title: Would you rather fall from a plane into snow, or into the ocean?
lines: This man fell three miles, and lived.
No parachute. Would you rather land in snow, or in the ocean?
Pick one right now, and comment A or B. Think fast.
First, the fall. In about fourteen seconds, you hit top speed.
About [120 mph](a hundred and twenty miles per hour). Almost twice highway speed.
Option B: the ocean. It sounds softer, right?
But water barely squeezes. At that speed, it hits almost like concrete.
Fall experts say water tends to knock people out.
And even if you survive the hit, you could drown.
Option A: snow. Fresh snow is up to [95%](ninety-five percent) air.
It squashes under you, so you slow down more gently.
And it's the sudden stop that kills you, not the fall.
Germany, March [1944](nineteen forty-four). A burning bomber, eighteen thousand feet up.
Tail gunner Nicholas [Alkemade's](Alkuhmahds) parachute is on fire. So he jumps without it.
Pine trees, then deep snow, break his fall.
He wakes up with a twisted knee. Not one broken bone.
In [1972](nineteen seventy-two), flight attendant Vesna [Vulović](Voolovitch) fell even farther.
Thirty-three thousand feet, higher than Mount Everest, inside a piece of her plane.
It came down on a snowy, wooded slope. Badly hurt, she survived.
Either way, survival is extremely rare. But by the science, option [A](eh) wins: the snow.
Snow is the reason why
